comparisons.peer_summary: Restructuring and other charges recognized in operating expenses were $1,533 million in fiscal year 2024 and $244 million in fiscal year 2023. The 2024 charges primarily consisted of employee termination costs related to cost reduction activities associated with the VMware Merger, while the 2023 charges were primarily non-recurring charges related to IP litigation.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom disclose significant charges impacting their operating results in 2024, though the nature and drivers differ. Intel reports $3.3 billion in non-cash impairments and accelerated depreciation for manufacturing assets and $1.3 billion in higher intersegment COGS. Broadcom reports $1,533 million in restructuring and other charges in operating expenses, primarily consisting of employee termination costs related to the VMware Merger. While Intel's charges are driven by asset obsolescence and manufacturing scale-up costs, Broadcom's are driven by integration costs from a major acquisition.

sentences.text: Cost of sales was $25.6 billion in 2024, up $4.1 billion from 2023, primarily driven by higher period charges related to non-cash impairments and accelerated depreciation of $3.3 billion for certain manufacturing assets, a substantial majority of which related to our Intel 7 process node; higher intersegment cost of goods sold of $1.3 billion primarily driven by higher sales volume and higher costs from the ramp of advanced technologies; and higher period charges primarily related to factory start-up costs.
Restructuring and other charges recognized in operating expenses were $1,533 million and $244 million in fiscal years 2024 and 2023, respectively.
The fiscal year 2024 charges primarily included employee termination costs from cost reduction activities related to the VMware Merger.

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2023, the company implemented cost reduction measures including a restructuring plan that reduced headcount by approximately 15%, incurred $171 million in restructure charges, and achieved estimated quarterly savings of $130 million through 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose significant manufacturing-related cost drivers impacting their financials in 2024. Intel attributes a $4.1 billion increase in cost of sales primarily to $3.3 billion in non-cash impairments and accelerated depreciation for manufacturing assets (Intel 7 node) and factory start-up costs. In contrast, Micron discloses that in 2023 it incurred $171 million in restructure charges to reduce costs, yielding estimated savings of $130 million per quarter (60% in COGS) through 2024, and notes in 2024 it phased out temporary cost-saving measures implemented in 2023. While both companies address manufacturing cost structures, Intel's disclosure highlights substantial non-cash write-downs and ramp-up costs increasing COGS, whereas Micron's disclosure focuses on prior-year restructuring efforts aimed at reducing COGS and the subsequent phase-out of those measures as market conditions improved.

sentences.text: Cost of sales was $25.6 billion in 2024, up $4.1 billion from 2023, primarily driven by higher period charges related to non-cash impairments and accelerated depreciation of $3.3 billion for certain manufacturing assets, a substantial majority of which related to our Intel 7 process node; higher intersegment cost of goods sold of $1.3 billion primarily driven by higher sales volume and higher costs from the ramp of advanced technologies; and higher period charges primarily related to factory start-up costs.
We incurred restructure charges of $171 million in 2023 primarily related to employee severance costs.

The 2023 Restructure Plan, which was substantially completed in 2023, yielded estimated cost savings of approximately $130 million per quarter (approximately 60% in cost of goods sold, 30% in R&D, and 10% in SG&A) subsequent to 2023.
In connection with improved 2024 market conditions, we reinstated our bonuses and phased out certain other temporary cost-saving measures that were implemented in 2023.
